terms.comment: In Lewis & Short temperātūra means due measure or temperament (ante-classical and post-Augustan), so calor is the safer word for heat.

phrases.latin: Temperātūra lāpsa est subter duōs et trīgintā gradūs.
phrases.english: The temperature fell below thirty-two degrees.

phrases.latin: Temperātūra est ad duōs gradūs suprā pūnctum glaciāle.
phrases.english: The temperature is two degrees above freezing.

phrases.latin: Temperātūra lāpsa est īnfrā pūnctum glaciāle; lacūnae concrēvērunt.
phrases.english: It’s gone below zero; the puddles have frozen.

sources: Lewis & Short: calor · Lewis & Short: temperatura
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. temperature.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 136, 392.
